title: Stress and Wellbeing Check-in
summary: A short check-in on worry, mood, daily pressure, sleep and support, designed to open a conversation in session.
clinicianNotes: Topic areas are informed by published work on measuring depression, anxiety and stress. All items are original wording and are not copied or adapted from any instrument. Bands are provisional and not clinically validated. Use the summary to guide your own questions. Draft content: needs review by a licensed psychologist before use with patients.
prompt: Thinking about the last two weeks, how true is this for you?

domains.label: Worry and tension
domains.description: Racing thoughts, expecting the worst, and physical tension.

guidance.ok: Worry and tension look manageable. Ask what helps, and whether anything has changed recently.
guidance.watch: Some worry and tension is showing. Explore triggers, how it shows up in the body, and what the person already does to cope.
guidance.explore: Worry and tension are prominent. Explore how long this has lasted, how it affects daily life, and whether a structured assessment is warranted.

domains.label: Mood and energy
domains.description: Enjoyment, low or flat feelings, and effort needed for everyday tasks.

guidance.ok: Mood and energy look steady. Ask about what gives the person energy and meaning.
guidance.watch: Some lowering of mood or energy is showing. Explore when it began, what changed, and how it affects routines and relationships.
guidance.explore: Mood and energy are strongly affected. Explore duration, impact on functioning, and whether a structured assessment is warranted.

domains.label: Daily pressure
domains.description: Feeling stretched by responsibilities, irritability, and little time to rest.

guidance.ok: Daily pressure looks manageable. Ask how the person protects time to rest.
guidance.watch: Pressure is building. Explore the main sources, what can be shared or reduced, and what the person feels they cannot change.
guidance.explore: The person feels overloaded. Explore practical relief, boundaries, and the effect on temper, health and relationships.

domains.label: Sleep and body
domains.description: Difficulty sleeping, unrefreshing sleep, and changes in appetite.

guidance.ok: Sleep and body routines look steady. Ask what supports good sleep.
guidance.watch: Sleep or appetite is being disturbed. Explore patterns, caffeine and screen habits, worry at night, and any recent change.
guidance.explore: Sleep or appetite is significantly disturbed. Explore duration and impact, and consider a medical review alongside psychological support.

domains.label: Support and strengths
domains.description: People to talk to, calming activities and coping resources. Higher is stronger.

guidance.ok: Support and strengths look solid. Build on them when planning next steps.
guidance.watch: Support is partly in place. Explore who is available, who is missing, and what the person already does that helps.
guidance.explore: Support looks thin. Prioritise connection, practical help and identifying safe people in the plan.

items.text: I find it hard to switch my mind off from worries.
My body feels tense or on edge, for example tight shoulders or a racing heart.
I expect things to go wrong more often than they actually do.
Things I usually enjoy feel less enjoyable.
I feel flat, heavy or low for much of the day.
Starting everyday tasks takes much more effort than it used to.
I have had thoughts that life is not worth living, or of harming myself.
My responsibilities feel like more than I can manage.
I get short-tempered or irritated more easily than usual.
I have very little time to rest or do things for myself.
I have trouble falling asleep or staying asleep.
I wake up tired even after a full night in bed.
My appetite or eating habits have changed in a way that worries me.
I have someone I can talk to about personal matters.
I still make time for something that calms me or gives me purpose.
When things get hard, I usually find a way to cope.
